title: Phosphatidylcholine to trimethylamine N-oxide
compartment: Intestinal lumen and gut bacteria, then hepatocyte endoplasmic reticulum

steps.note: Releases the sn-2 fatty acid; much of the product is absorbed and reacylated

steps.enzyme: Choline trimethylamine-lyase CutC, activated by CutD (gut bacteria)
cofactors: Glycyl radical, generated by CutD from S-adenosylmethionine
steps.note: Cleaves the C–N bond; also yields acetaldehyde
Hepatic; TMAO is excreted in urine; FMO3 deficiency causes trimethylaminuria
